description: The bar chart, titled "Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models," displays the number of tasks associated with various language families and individual languages, with the horizontal axis representing the number of tasks (labeled "# tasks") on a linear scale from 0 to 80, and the vertical axis listing the language categories. The data reveals a wide disparity in the number of tasks across the different linguistic groups. The IE-Slavic language family has the highest number of tasks, with a bar extending to approximately 79. The IE-Romance family follows with about 47 tasks, and the IE-Germanic family has around 44 tasks. The Uralic family has approximately 20 tasks, while the IE-Baltic family has about 17. The IE-other category has roughly 15 tasks, and the IE-Indic family has about 10. The Semitic language has approximately 8 tasks, the Turkic language has about 5, and the Basque language has the fewest, with approximately 4 tasks. The bars are sorted in descending order of the number of tasks, with the longest bar at the top and the shortest at the bottom.
